newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline drifts higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline drifts higher.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices drifted higher on Thursday, tracking modest gains in NYMEX unleaded futures prices, traders said.
Midwest diesel fuel prices moved lower, also tracking the underlying futures contracts in thin trade in the Group Three and Chicago markets, traders said.
Gasoline and diesel differentials remained largely unaffected by shipping delays on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system that pushed liftings back by five days earlier this week.
"There's nothing going on," said one trader, who said some activity was being generated by traders closing out May positions in the futures market.
Chicago unleaded gasoline differentials were steady at bids 0.25 cent a gallon under to even with NYMEX May unleaded, while Group Three remained 0.50/0.25 cent under the print, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was unchanged at 6.0/6.25 cents over NYMEX May heating oil, with Group Three also steady at 2.50/2.75 cents over the print.
High sulphur also was talked unchanged at bids 1.50 cents over the print in Chicago and 5.75 cents over the print in Group Three.
